data.name: Ursula
data.gender_notes: Ursula is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'ursa', meaning 'bear'. Named after the legendary saint and martyr, Ursula of Cologne, who was said to have been a bear in a previous life and saved countless souls before her death. The name Ursula carries the meaning “Little Female Bear” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ursula usually hope their child will grow to embody little female bear and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of strength and protection, embodying the motherly and nurturing qualities of a bear.
data.etymology: Ursula belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little Female Bear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ursula total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: אורסולה
in_hebrew.meaning: לשון שור Ursola שמות הנוצרים הקדושים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אורסולה היא שם נוצרי שמקורו בלטינית ומשמעותו 'דוב קטן'. השם נגזר מהמילה הלטינית 'ursa', שפירושה 'דוב'. השם אורסולה היה נפוץ בקרב הנוצרים הקדושים והפך פופולרי בימי הביניים. הוא קשור לסנטה אורסולה, קדושה נוצרית מהמאה ה-4 לספירה.

in_greek.name: Ουρσουλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ουρσουλα προέρχεται από το λατινικό 'ursa', που σημαίνει 'αρκούδα'. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν δημοφιλές στους πρώτους Χριστιανούς και συνδέεται με την Αγία Ουρσουλα, μια Χριστιανή αγία του 4ου αιώνα μ.Χ. που ήταν γνωστή για την ευσέβειά της και την θυσία της.

in_latin.name: Ursula
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Ursula is derived from the Latin word 'ursa', meaning 'bear'. It was a popular name among early Christians and became associated with Saint Ursula, a 4th-century Christian martyr and saint. The name symbolizes strength and courage, reflecting the bear's powerful nature.

in_english.name: Ursula
in_english.meaning: Little bear, symbolizing strength and courage
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ursula originates from the Latin 'ursa', meaning 'bear'. It was popularized by Saint Ursula, a 4th-century Christian martyr. The name signifies strength, courage, and resilience, reflecting the characteristics of a bear. Throughout Christian tradition, Ursula has been a celebrated name, embodying the virtues of its eponymous saint.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ursula, derived from the Latin word 'ursa' meaning 'bear', has been used throughout history in various cultures. In medieval Europe, Ursula was a popular feminine given name, and she was linked to the legend of the Ursula and the Eleven Thousand Virgins, a group of young women who were martyred for their faith. In the Catholic Church, Ursula is venerated as a virgin and martyr, her feast day celebrated on October 21.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Ursula holds deep spiritual significance, as it is linked to the life and legacy of Saint Ursula, who was believed to have been a bear in a previous life before being born as a human. According to legend, Ursula was a British princess who lived in the 4th or 5th century, and she was renowned for her great beauty and piety. She was offered in marriage to the pagan king of Huns, but refused, and instead, she and her companions embarked on a pilgrimage to Rome. Along the way, they encountered the Huns, but instead of submitting to the king's demands, they all chose to die rather than abandon their faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ursula, derived from the Latin word 'ursus' meaning bear, represents strength, endurance, and nurturing qualities. In Christian tradition, St. Ursula is believed to have led an army of virgin warriors, embodying both feminine force and martyrdom.
